result: In 19 severe ME/CFS patients a 15-min 20-degree tilt reduced extracranial CBF by a mean 27%, comparable to the 26% fall seen in milder patients on a 30-min 70-degree tilt.
reason: Same measure and group (not an independent cohort, no controls); adds severe subgroup and a milder tilt protocol, so extends not replicates. Different paper from the 429-patient van Campen 2020 cited study.

reason: Qualitative review of existing cohorts, not an independent cohort or effect-size analysis; consistent with the cohort-specific, inconsistent picture, so extends at most.

result: In 305 ME/CFS vs 201 controls, PTPN22 rs2476601 (OR 1.63) and CTLA4 rs3087243 (OR 1.53) risk alleles were associated with ME/CFS only in infection-triggered onset, not in non-infectious onset (OR 1.09 and 0.89).
reason: Covered by the newer finding genetics-ptpn22-ctla4, which this paper likely underlies (check whether already cited).

result: In 920 women, tender-point dolorimetry pain thresholds were lower in CFS without FM (5.8 kg), CFS/FM (3.1 kg), FM (3.9 kg) and GWI (2.9 kg) than in sedentary controls (7.2 kg, p<0.0001); thresholds did not correlate with symptoms in CFS.
reason: Independent cohort, pressure pain thresholds, same direction for generalised hyperalgesia; separates CFS-only from CFS/FM, addressing the FM confound.

result: Only 1 of 161 ME/CFS patients had anti-PDC autoantibodies (vs 15/15 PBC); anti-mitochondrial membrane antibodies were negative and anti-cardiolipin did not differ from controls.
reason: Does not measure PDH function, so cannot contradict it; rules out anti-PDC autoantibodies as the cause of the proposed PDH block.
